headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 8 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.74 (95% CI: 0.56–0.99), suggesting that selenium is associated with a lower risk of bladder cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 74.09%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.

sample_size.excerpt: The association between toenail selenium status and subsequent bladder cancer incidence was investigated in a prospective cohort study among 120,852 men and women aged 55-69 years at baseline (September 1986).

cases.excerpt: Follow-up for incident cancer was established by record linkage to cancer registries until December 1992. The multivariable case-cohort analysis was based on 431 bladder cancer cases and 2,459 subcohort members, for whom toenail selenium levels were available.

effect_size.excerpt: The age-, sex- and smoking-adjusted rate ratios (95% confidence intervals) for increasing quintiles of toenail selenium were 1.00 (reference), 1.09 (0.80-1.48), 0.55 (0.38-0.79), 0.63 (0.43-0.91), and 0.67 (0.46-0.97), respectively (P-trend < 0.01).

sample_size.excerpt: Source documentation was obtained on 229 cases. Upon review 3 patients were excluded from analysis because they were misreported as bladder cancer, and 2 were excluded due to insufficient source documentation to confirm the diagnosis, leaving 224 bladder cancer among the 34,887 eligible, evaluable SELECT participants.( 18 ) Of the 35,533 men who were randomized 646 were excluded from all analyses, including 10 due to prior diagnosis of prostate cancer (in another the diagnosis was discovered after primary publication) and 15 who never received proper informed consent, while all 621 participants from 2 clinical sites were excluded due to severe data and participant management problems.

cases.excerpt: Table 1 lists the characteristics of the 224 men with and the 34,663 without bladder cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: The bladder cancer rate was higher in the 3 treatment arms than in the placebo arm but no difference was statistically significant (vitamin E HR 1.06, 99% CI 0.72 – 1.53, selenium HR 1.13, 99% CI 0.78–1.63, vitamin E plus selenium HR 1.05, 99% CI 0.71 – 1.51).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The bladder cancer rate was higher in the 3 treatment arms than in the placebo arm but no difference was statistically significant (vitamin E HR 1.06, 99% CI 0.72 – 1.53, selenium HR 1.13, 99% CI 0.78–1.63, vitamin E plus selenium HR 1.05, 99% CI 0.71 – 1.51).

studies.Title: Variation of urinary and serum trace elements (Ca, Zn, Cu, Se) in bladder carcinoma in China.
studies.Reference: Variation of urinary and serum trace elements (Ca, Zn, Cu, Se) in bladder carcinoma in China.
studies.Journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
studies.Population: Patients with bladder carcinoma and healthy persons in China
studies.comparison_type: cases versus healthy controls (serum selenium levels)

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: To determine this, 81 patients with bladder carcinoma chosen as a study group and 130 healthy persons chosen as a control group were all assayed for urinary and serum trace elements (calcium [Ca], zinc [Zn], copper [Cu], selenium [Se]) using an atomic absorption spectrophotometer, and the results were analyzed by independent sample t tests.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: Since there are few studies of the effect of trace elements in bladder carcinoma in China, the aim of this study was thus to assess variation using a case control approach. To determine this, 81 patients with bladder carcinoma chosen as a study group and 130 healthy persons chosen as a control group were all assayed for urinary and serum trace elements (calcium [Ca], zinc [Zn], copper [Cu], selenium [Se]) using an atomic absorption spectrophotometer, and the results were analyzed by independent sample t tests.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: Serum Ca and Se levels of study group were significantly lower (P<0.05) than those of control group.
